Hi Ellen — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a compact packet to start: ppq-fill.pdf (answers to your PPQ items) and dataflow-v1.png (annotated dataflow). A few notes inline below.

1) PII classification mapping (short):
- Sensitive (PHI-equivalent): appointment_notes, diagnostics, free-text clinical notes — stored encrypted at rest, masked in telemetry by default.
- Restricted: patient_id, payment identifiers — persistent identifiers, access-controlled, KMS-wrapped.
- Internal: non-identifying metadata, routing headers — retained for 30 days in aggregated form.

2) Subprocessors: primary list included in the attached ppq-fill.pdf. Short summary here:
- Redwood KMS (managed): key custody is split; customer keys can be BYOK via KMS integrations.
- Telemetry-Processor (third party): receives anonymized token-level metrics; we apply token redaction and prefix hashing before telemetry export.
- Analytics / billing (vendor): invoice-level aggregates only; no raw prompts.

Ive highlighted the KMS custody and telemetry controls in the ppq document. For each subprocessor we included the role, jurisdiction, and a 1-2 sentence custody note.

3) Transfers & annex: Redwood can execute either a custom binding annex or standard SCCs depending on your procurement preference. For HealthGrid we typically offer a binding transfer annex (we have a template) when customers require contractual clarity on routing and audit logs. Ive attached the draft annex_draft.pdf (see later message) but note that legal will want to iterate on a few paragraphs about exporter/importer liabilities.

4) Artifacts: dataflow-v1.png is the annotated diagram; ppq-fill.pdf contains the roster and short exhibits. We can also produce a logs-export example and KMS attestation on request.

Next steps: if this looks good I suggest we schedule a 30-min call with your security/legal to walk the annex points and confirm procurement formality.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Ellen — short answers below and links to evidence. Ill bring Marissa into procurement scoping once you confirm.

- Telemetry-Processor: does NOT receive raw prompts. We stream token-level metrics after in-line redaction and prefix hashing. The pipeline applies three protections: prefix stripping for the first N tokens of a prompt (configurable), dynamic redaction for sequences matching PII regexes, and one-way hashing for non-PII metadata. We documented the flow in dataflow-v1.png (labels: "redaction node", "hash node").

- KMS custody attestation: customer-managed keys (BYOK) are supported via KMS integrations. Attestation: Redwoods key agent never exports plaintext key material. Key handles are passed to the runtime; all wrapping/unwrapping occurs within the customer's KMS (or within HSM when used). We can provide a signed attestation from our security team if you need a formal artifact.

- Audit logs example: JSON schema below (we can produce a CSV export sample):
{
  "timestamp": "2028-06-18T15:19:02Z",
  "actor_id": "service-account:healthgrid-ingest",
  "action": "model.generate",
  "resource": "model/redwood-13b/v1:request/abcd1234",
  "result": "accepted",
  "notes": "redaction:applied, kms:key-handle:hex..."
}

Ive added the link to a shared Drive folder with the ppq answers and a short KMS attestation draft: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-example

If that satisfies your auditors, Marissa can open the procurement request and Laura can finalize the annex draft. Happy to do a quick 20-min walk-through.

Thanks,
Jordan
